extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system; mathematicians implementing Ore-localizations and real singularity classification
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the SINGULAR libraries olga.lib (Ore-localization in G-Algebras) and realclassify.lib (classification of real isolated hypersurface singularities). Describes data formats, validity checks, procedure semantics, assumptions and examples for using these libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization types (Type 0/1/2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current localization types: Type 0: monoidal - represented by a list of polys g1,...,gk that have to be contained in a commutative polynomial subring of A generated by a subset of the variables of A. Type 1: geometric - only for algebras with an even number of variables where the first half induces a commutative polynomial subring B; represented by an ideal p, which has to be a prime ideal in B. Type 2: rational - represented by an intvec v = [i1,...,ik] in the range 1..nvars(basering). Localization data is an int specifying the type and a def with the corresponding information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate representation type for the localization. For monoidal supply a list of polynomials; for geometric supply an ideal in the commutative first-half variables (prime in B); for rational supply an intvec of variable indices. See paper reference for more examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraction representation format
rubrics_metrics.description: A fraction is represented as a vector with four entries: [s,r,p,t]. Here, s^{-1}r is the left fraction representation, pt^{-1} is the right one. If s or t is zero, the corresponding representation is not set. If both are zero, the fraction is not valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always fill the left or right representation as needed. Procedures in olga.lib expect this vector format; many checks verify denominators and equality of left/right representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: locStatus return semantics and basic checks
rubrics_metrics.description: locStatus(locType, locData) returns a list: the first entry is 0 or 1 depending whether the input represents a valid localization; the second entry is a string with a status/error message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call locStatus to determine validity before using locData. Expect detailed error strings for incorrect types, undefined data, or type mismatches; examples in the manual illustrate many common error messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoidal localization requirements (validation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a monoidal localization (type 0), locData must be of type list and a non-empty list of polys/ints/numbers; the variables occurring in the polys in locData have to induce a commutative polynomial subring of basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: locStatus and related procedures will report errors if locData is not a list, is empty, contains wrong types, or the listed polynomials use variables that do not form a commutative subring. Use normalizeMonoidal to factor and canonicalize monoidal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric localization requirements (validation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a geometric localization (type 1), basering must have an even number of variables whose first half induces a commutative polynomial subring B; locData has to be of type ideal and an ideal generated by polynomials containing only variables from the first half; p should be a prime ideal in B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the ring ordering/variable grouping places the commutative variables in the first half. locStatus will error if locData is not an ideal, uses wrong variables, or if the base ring does not meet the even-variable commutativity condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational localization requirements (validation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a rational localization (type 2), locData must be of type intvec, non-zero, and each index must be in the range 1..nvars(basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: normalizeRational(v) purges duplicate entries and sorts the intvec. locStatus/testLocData will error for strings/wrong types or zero-length vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: testLocData behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: testLocData(locType, locData) tests if the given data specifies a denominator set with respect to the checks from locStatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: testLocData throws an error if checks were not successful; use it to enforce denominators are acceptable before proceeding with fraction/arithmetic operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInS: membership in denominator set
rubrics_metrics.description: isInS(p, locType, locData(, override)) returns 0 or 1 depending whether polynomial p is in the denominator set specified by locType and locData. If override is set, it will not normalize locData (use with care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use isInS to check whether a polynomial can serve as a denominator for a given localization. Examples show expected behavior for monoidal, geometric and rational localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: fracStatus: fraction validity checks and messages
rubrics_metrics.description: fracStatus(frac, locType, locData) determines if the given vector is a representation of a fraction in the specified localization and returns a list: the first entry is 0 or 1 indicating validity; the second entry is a status string. Checks include: a valid localization type, denominators specified, left and right denominators belonging to the denominator set, and equality of left and right representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the returned status string to diagnose why a fraction vector is invalid (e.g. missing denominators, denominators not in S, left/right representations not equal).

rubrics_metrics.name: testFraction: enforced validation
rubrics_metrics.description: testFraction(frac, locType, locData) performs the checks from fracStatus and throws an error if the checks were not successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use testFraction to abort computation early when fraction representation is invalid rather than manually checking fracStatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: leftOre / rightOre semantics and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: leftOre(s, r, locType, locData) computes left Ore data for a given tuple (s,r) assuming s is in the denominator set; it returns a list whose first entry is a vector [ts,tr] such that ts*r = tr*s and whose second entry describes all choices for ts. rightOre(s, r, locType, locData) analogously computes [ts,tr] such that r*ts = s*tr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use leftOre/rightOre to compute the necessary multipliers to move factors across numerators/denominators in noncommutative Ore localizations. The procedures return explicit ts,tr and examples verify correctness by checking the indicated equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: convertRightToLeftFraction / convertLeftToRightFraction behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: convertRightToLeftFraction(frac, locType, locData) determines a left fraction representation of a given fraction; convertLeftToRightFraction does the converse. If the requested representation is already specified, the fraction is returned unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conversions use Ore-data computations and respect the localization's denominator set; examples show returned vectors and verification that rm[2]*g - rm[1]*f == 0 (consistency checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: addLeftFractions / multiplyLeftFractions semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: addLeftFractions(a, b, locType, locData(, override)) returns a vector representing the sum of two left fractions as a fraction in the specified localization. multiplyLeftFractions(a, b, locType, locData(, override)) returns a vector representing their product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The returned vectors are canonical fraction representations of the sum/product in the localization. Use the procedures to perform arithmetic in the localized ring; examples demonstrate monoidal, geometric and rational cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: areEqualLeftFractions equality test
rubrics_metrics.description: areEqualLeftFractions(a, b, locType, locData) returns 1 or 0 depending on whether vectors a and b represent equal fractions in the specified localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to test fraction equality after arithmetic or conversions; examples show nontrivial cases where fractions with different numerators/denominators compare equal or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInvertibleLeftFraction check (conservative)
rubrics_metrics.description: isInvertibleLeftFraction(frac, locType, locData) returns 1 if the numerator of frac is in the denominator set, and returns 0 otherwise. NOTE: a return value 0 does NOT mean the fraction is not invertible; it just means it could not be determined by this method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conservative test for invertibility; a positive result (1) implies invertibility, a negative result is inconclusive and may require additional methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: invertLeftFraction behavior (constructive/informative)
rubrics_metrics.description: invertLeftFraction(frac, locType, locData) returns the multiplicative inverse of frac in the specified localization if frac is invertible according to the procedure; it throws an error if frac is not invertible (again noting this does not prove non-invertibility in general).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after isInvertibleLeftFraction or when you know a fraction is invertible. The procedure may fail with an error when it cannot construct an inverse even if one exists abstractly.

rubrics_metrics.name: isZeroFraction / isOneFraction predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: isZeroFraction(frac) returns 1 if frac == 0 and 0 otherwise; isOneFraction(frac) returns 1 if frac == 1 and 0 otherwise. Assumption: frac is a valid fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These predicates test normalized fraction vectors for equality with 0 or 1. Ensure fracStatus/testFraction passed before using them.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalizeMonoidal behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: normalizeMonoidal(L) computes a normal form of monoidal localization data: given a list of polys, returns a list of all unique factors appearing in the given polys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use normalizeMonoidal to canonicalize and simplify monoidal locData before passing to other procedures; examples show factor extraction and deduplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalizeRational behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: normalizeRational(v) computes a normal form of rational localization data: purges duplicate entries and sorts ascendingly, returning an intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call normalizeRational to canonicalize rational locData (intvec) to ensure consistent behavior across procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: testOlga / testOlgaExamples utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: testOlga() executes a series of internal testing procedures. testOlgaExamples() executes the examples of all procedures in this library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run these to validate the installed olga.lib functions on your system and to see example runs; useful during development or debugging of the library environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: realclassify output structure (NormalFormEquation keys)
rubrics_metrics.description: realclassify(f) returns a list NF of elements of type NormalFormEquation with keys: NF.singularityType (string), NF.normalFormEquation (Poly), NF.modality, NF.parameters (list of [parameter_term, interval]), NF.corank (int), NF.inertiaIndex (int), NF.milnorNumber (int), NF.determinacy (a lower bound int).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect these keys to understand the classification result. Examples in the manual show typical outputs for many ADE and exceptional types and how modality/parameters are represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: realclassify assumptions and input requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification is done over the real numbers. The ground field must be Q (the rational numbers). No field extensions nor floating point numbers are allowed. The monomial order must be local. The input polynomial must be contained in maxideal(2) and must be an isolated singularity of modality 0 or 1. The Milnor number is checked for being finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your ring and polynomial satisfy these preconditions before calling realclassify. If modality>1 or the singularity is not isolated, the procedure may not be applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: realclassify modality=1 parameter representation
rubrics_metrics.description: In case NF.modality = 1, the parameter values are given as an element of a number field QQ[a]/(minpoly); the coefficient ring of NF.normalFormEquation uses the unique root of minpoly in the interval specified in NF.parameters in conjunction with the parameter term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modality=1, interpret NF.parameters entries as [parameter_term, interval] together with NF.minimal_polynomial (minpoly) describing the algebraic parameter; the valid real root is selected according to the interval. Examples show output fields: Parameter term, Minimal polynomial, Interval.
